label: The old high altar
blurb: Reredos, tabernacle at the center, six candles, the marble the parish paid for in 1924.

label: The 1970s sanctuary
blurb: A freestanding altar, carpet, a plain wooden cross, the reredos long gone.

label: A modern sanctuary
blurb: Stone, glass, a single line of light. Architects will photograph it; the old guard will not forgive it.

label: A restored sanctuary
blurb: Put back what was taken out, with the marble found in the basement. A long argument and a beautiful result.

label: Gothic revival
blurb: Pointed arches painted on, a carved wooden reredos, blue and gold. A choice that tells everyone what you read.

label: No altar rail
blurb: Removed in 1971 and not missed by everyone.

label: A wooden altar rail
blurb: Oak, kneelers, a gate. People will kneel for Communion whether you ask them to or not.

label: A marble altar rail
blurb: Salvaged from a closed church across the diocese. Heavy, permanent, and a statement.

label: Facing the people
blurb: The freestanding altar, the priest facing the nave. What everyone under sixty grew up with.

label: Ad orientem
blurb: Priest and people facing the same way. Cheap in money, expensive in everything else; the chancery will hear within the week.

label: The old booths
blurb: Two dark boxes with a screen and a kneeler. Anonymous, and the line is longer for it.

label: A reconciliation room
blurb: Two chairs, a screen you can ignore, a box of tissues. Some will never use it.

label: Both
blurb: A booth for those who want the screen and a room for those who want a face. Costs a side aisle.

label: The choir loft
blurb: Up and behind, with the organ. Heard, not seen.

label: An ensemble up front
blurb: Guitars and a keyboard beside the ambo, microphones, a leader who waves.

label: A schola in the side chapel
blurb: Six voices, chant, no instruments. The music director will need to be someone else.

label: The statues, all of them
blurb: Every saint the founding families brought with them, with candles.

label: Mary and Joseph only
blurb: The rest to the basement or the side chapel. Cleaner, and someone will cry.

label: Bare walls
blurb: Nothing but the cross. The building becomes a room.

label: Tabernacle at the center
blurb: Behind the altar, where the eye goes first.

label: Tabernacle in a side chapel
blurb: A chapel of reservation, quiet, with its own door. The sanctuary is for the Mass.

label: A crucifix
blurb: The one from ordination, and nothing else.

label: A crucifix and an icon
blurb: Byzantine, gold ground, a gift from someone who knew what you liked.

label: The Holy Father's portrait
blurb: Framed, signed by no one, and read by every visitor as a position.

label: Photographs of the parish
blurb: First Communions, the festival, the men who built the hall.

label: The desk you were given
blurb: Scarred, enormous, older than the diocese.

label: A plain desk
blurb: From the catalog. Nothing to interpret.

label: A globe
blurb: For the missions, or for looking at.

label: A plant the secretary waters
blurb: It will outlive your assignment.

label: Filing cabinets
blurb: Three, locked, the parish's memory.

label: A crucifix over the table
blurb: As in every rectory in the diocese.

label: Family photographs
blurb: Your people, on the wall where you eat.

label: A prayer corner
blurb: A kneeler, an icon, a lamp. The pastor pretends not to notice.

label: A television
blurb: The game on Sunday afternoons, the news you should not watch.

label: A reading chair and a lamp
blurb: Where the evenings go.
